title: The Fort Dearborn monument's five figures take the sculpture's poses
items: The bronze group on 18th Street now stands as Rohl-Smith posed it: the warrior in a long lunge with the tomahawk raised, Mrs. Helm staggering back with her arm across to him, Black Partridge behind her with his open hand raised against the blow and his musket slanting past his hip, the surgeon fallen under them, and the child kneeling at the front with both arms out.
Each figure's joints were read off the Barnes-Crosby photograph of about 1900 and set in depth using J. W. Taylor's 1893 view, so the group's outline from the walk now follows the photograph.
The cast rock under their feet is rough and broken, as in both photographs, where it used to be a smooth swell.
Still to do: faces, hair, drapery and weapons are not yet modelled, and the inscription is not yet cut.
